## Security rules (Security Kit)

This project follows a tailored security plan for **security-kit** in `.seckit/SECURITY-PLAN.md`.
These rules are requirements, not suggestions. Apply them whenever you write, change or review code.

- If a request would break a rule, say so and propose a compliant alternative instead of silently complying.
- When code implements or touches a control, mention its ID (e.g. `AUTH-C2`) in the summary or PR description.
- For the full reasoning and verification steps, read the control in `.seckit/SECURITY-PLAN.md` or run `npx seckit explain <ID>`.
- If the `seckit` MCP server is connected: call `get_controls_for_file` before editing a file and `check_code` on new or changed code before finishing.
- Never add or change entries in `.seckit/attestations.yaml`; sign-offs are made by people.

### Authentication

- **AUTH-C2** (critical): Hash passwords only with Argon2id from a maintained library (bcrypt or scrypt if unavailable); never use MD5/SHA-* for passwords and never store or log a plaintext password.
- **AUTH-C1** (high): Every login, OTP-verification and password-reset endpoint must be rate-limited per account and per IP; never write an authentication endpoint without throttling.
- **AUTH-C3** (high): Password policy: minimum 12 characters, maximum at least 64, no composition rules, and reject passwords found in breach lists; validate on the server, not only the client.
- **AUTH-C5** (high): On successful login or privilege change, regenerate the session ID / issue new tokens and invalidate the previous session.
- **AUTH-C7** (high): One-time codes: generate with a CSPRNG, expire in 10 minutes or less, single use, invalidate after 5 failed attempts, compare in constant time.
- **AUTH-C8** (high): Design authentication so a second factor (passkey/WebAuthn or TOTP) can be enforced; admin accounts must always require MFA.
- **AUTH-C4** (medium): Login, signup and password-reset responses must not reveal whether an account exists: same message, same status code, comparable timing.
- **AUTH-C9** (medium): Never implement security questions or password hints for account recovery.

### Web frontend

- **WEB-C1** (critical): Never use innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, document.write, dangerouslySetInnerHTML, v-html, eval or new Function with dynamic data; rely on framework escaping, and sanitize with DOMPurify when HTML is unavoidable.
- **WEB-C2** (high): Do not add inline scripts or event-handler attributes; scripts load from our origin or carry the CSP nonce; never add unsafe-inline or unsafe-eval to script-src.
- **WEB-C3** (high): Keep the security-headers middleware on every response (HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy) and never remove or weaken it.
- **WEB-C4** (high): Load every resource and call every API over https://; never hardcode http:// URLs except localhost in development.
- **WEB-C5** (medium): Prefer npm packages over CDN script tags; any external <script> must have integrity and crossorigin attributes unless the provider forbids SRI.
- **WEB-C6** (medium): Never redirect to a URL taken directly from user input; accept only relative paths starting with a single "/" or an allow-listed destination.
- **WEB-C8** (medium): Responses containing personal or sensitive data must send Cache-Control no-store.

### API

- **API-C1** (critical): Every handler that loads or changes a record by ID must check that the current user is allowed to access that specific record (scope the query by owner/tenant); being authenticated is not enough.
- **API-C2** (critical): Apply authorization middleware to all routes by default and explicitly mark public ones; check roles/permissions on the server for every privileged action, never only in the UI.
- **API-C3** (high): Validate every request with a schema that rejects unknown fields; never pass req.body directly to an ORM create/update; return explicit response objects, never whole database models.
- **API-C4** (high): List endpoints must enforce a maximum page size; apply rate limits, request body size limits and timeouts to all API routes.
- **API-C6** (high): Configure CORS with an explicit list of allowed origins; never reflect the request Origin, never allow "null", and never use "*" with credentials.
- **API-C11** (high): Third-party API credentials must be per-client, scoped to minimum permissions, stored hashed, revocable and rate-limited per client.
- **API-C8** (medium): API error responses must not include stack traces, SQL errors or internal paths; return a generic message with a request ID and log details server-side; disable X-Powered-By and debug modes.
- **API-C9** (medium): Document new endpoints in the API spec; do not add debug, test or temporary endpoints without removing them before merge.
- **API-C10** (medium): Accept API keys and tokens only from headers or cookies, never from query string parameters.

### Database

- **DB-C1** (critical): Never build SQL with string concatenation or template literals; always use bound parameters, and pick dynamic identifiers (columns, sort order) from an allow-list.
- **DB-C4** (critical): Never hardcode database credentials or connection strings; read them from environment variables or a secrets manager.
- **DB-C3** (high): The application connects with a least-privilege database user; migrations use a separate account; never connect as root/superuser/admin.
- **DB-C5** (high): Database connections must use TLS with certificate verification; never disable certificate checks (e.g. rejectUnauthorized: false, sslmode=require without verify).
- **DB-C6** (high): Sensitive fields (IDs, health, financial data) are encrypted at rest; keys come from a KMS, never from source code.

### File upload

- **UPLOAD-C1** (critical): Validate uploads by file content (magic bytes) against an allow-list of types; never trust the extension or client Content-Type; re-encode images server-side.
- **UPLOAD-C2** (high): Store uploads under a server-generated random name; never build a filesystem path or object key from the user-supplied file name.
- **UPLOAD-C4** (high): Store uploads in private object storage or a non-executable directory outside the web root; serve them via short-lived signed URLs or a controlled download handler.
- **UPLOAD-C5** (high): Serve user uploads from a separate domain with Content-Disposition: attachment (except safe images), explicit Content-Type and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff; never inline user SVG/HTML on the app origin.
- **UPLOAD-C3** (medium): Enforce a maximum upload size at the server, and cap decompressed size, entry count and image dimensions before processing any archive or image.
- **UPLOAD-C6** (medium): Quarantine uploads and make them available to other users only after a malware scan passes.

### Payments

- **PAY-C3** (critical): Payment webhooks must verify the provider signature on the raw request body with the webhook secret, reject stale timestamps, and ignore event IDs that were already processed.
- **PAY-C4** (critical): Never accept prices, totals or currency from the client; compute amounts on the server from the catalog and verify the paid amount and currency before fulfilling an order.
- **PAY-C2** (high): Never log, persist or send to analytics any card number, CVV or full payment payload; store only provider IDs plus brand and last 4 digits.
- **PAY-C5** (high): Create charges with idempotency keys and make order fulfilment idempotent (unique constraint or transaction on the payment ID) so it can never run twice.
- **PAY-C7** (medium): Rate-limit payment and card-setup attempts per user, IP and card fingerprint, and keep the provider's fraud screening enabled.
